title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 223 (Agent to be indemnified against consequences of acts done in good faith)

content.overview: Section 223 provides that where one person employs another to do an act, and the agent does the act in good faith, the employer is liable to indemnify the agent against the consequences of that act, though it may cause an injury to the rights of third persons.
content.glance: Act done in good faith for the employer → employer indemnifies agent even if third-party rights are injured (subject to s. 224).
content.study: Where one person employs another to do an act, and the agent does the act in good faith, the employer is liable to indemnify the agent against the consequences of that act, though it may cause an injury to the rights of third persons. Illustrations: (a) decree-holder directs court officer to seize goods as B’s; true owner C sues the officer — A must indemnify the officer; (b) B sells goods in A’s possession at A’s request without knowing A had no right; true owner recovers from B — A must indemnify B. Read with s. 222 (lawful acts within authority) and s. 224 (no indemnity for criminal acts).

sections.heading: Indemnity despite injury to third persons
sections.body: The employer is liable to indemnify the agent against the consequences, though the act may injure third-party rights.

provisions.title: Agent to be indemnified against consequences of acts done in good faith

examples.title: Statutory illustration — seizure of goods
examples.body: A directs a court officer to seize goods as B’s. The officer seizes them in good faith and is sued by the true owner C. A must indemnify the officer.

examples.title: Statutory illustration — sale without title
examples.body: B sells goods in A’s possession at A’s request, not knowing A had no right. True owner recovers from B. A must indemnify B.

hypotheticals.question: Does good faith alone always secure indemnity?
hypotheticals.analysis: Good faith is required under s. 223, but s. 224 bars indemnity where the act employed is criminal.

distinctions.title: Good-faith acts injuring third parties (s. 223) vs lawful acts within authority (s. 222)
distinctions.left: Good faith; may injure third-party rights
distinctions.right: Lawful acts in exercise of conferred authority

misconceptions.trap: The agent always bears loss when a third party is injured.
misconceptions.correction: Section 223 shifts the consequences to the employer when the agent acted in good faith.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 223 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify employment and the act. II. Test good faith. III. Apply indemnity despite injury to third persons. IV. Check s. 224 crime bar. V. Conclude.
